newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower in mixed trade.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower in mixed trade.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly lower Thursday, continuing the drift lower of the past week and half.

"After doing nothing much all day, we saw some commission house selling near the close, with silver, which has been the strongest in the complex, looking like it is now on the retreat also," Pell Brothers floor trader Don Tierney said.
COMEX December silver ended down 3.7 cents at $5.193, after seeing a two week intraday low at $5.155.
COMEX December gold ended down 10 cents at $389.60 an ounce, after trading in a $390.40-389.30 range.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted $385.50/386.00 at the close, from a London afternoon fix Thursday at $386.00, compared to a Wednesday close in New York at $385.50/386.00

"We've had a small war in the Middle East, the U.S. economy remains strong, but precious metals are finding little support from either factor," North American Equity Services floor trader John Geraghty said.
"It looks like we are going to probe lower levels, but we understand there are some producer buybacks likely at slightly lower levels," he said.
The U.S. economy and financial market conditions are not supportive of buying gold at this point, analysts said.
U.S treasury bond prices fell further Thursday on news U.S. weekly jobless claims fell 15,000 to 316,000, compared to consensus forecasts for a 4,000 rise.

The news supported the view the U.S. labor market remained strong, one day prior to the release of key August U.S. payrolls data, which might prompt the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, analysts said.
But analysts still expect precious metals to see only limited downside as fabrication demand pick up again after the traditional summer lull.
In the platinum metals group, NYMEX October platinum ended down 90 cents at $396.10 an ounce, while NYMEX December palladium ended up 15 cents at $126.75.
